label: input s at a late original position (t >= 5)
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, when the input token is the letter s at position t >= 5 (a few weak firings at t = 4). It never fires on any other token, on s at t <= 3, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (even when s is fed back as an output). Magnitude rises with position: s at t = 5 gives about 0.4 of max, and s at t = 7 gives the top activations (about 1.0). Within one sequence, repeated s tokens at later positions activate more strongly. Preceding tokens, the first token and digit count have no clear effect.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split there are 0 false positives, so every s input at t>=5 in the original phase fires. All 772 misses are weak firings (about 0.02-0.07 of max) on s at t=4, and together they hold only 0.1% of activation mass. In the dev profile, 743 of the roughly 17k s tokens at t=4 fire, so these are sparse rather than a separate class worth adding.
Widening the predicate to t>=4 gets recall 1.0 but drops precision to 0.68 (F1 0.81), so the original t>=5 cutoff is the better choice.
The claims about where it fires hold: zero activity at the delimiter, in the copy phase, at t<=3 and on any non-s token, and out_tok=s gives no firing in the copy phase.

Small overclaims: magnitude at t=8 is about the same as at t=7 (mass per firing about 0.046 vs 0.048, while the top examples all sit at t=7), so 'peaks at t=7' is really 'saturates at t>=7'. The claim that repeated s tokens fire more strongly is mostly explained by position: a later s is also at a larger t. Neither changes the label.
